title: Close detached Runner recovery and tmux delivery races
objective: Correct the rejected detached execution implementation so Runner ownership fails closed when the worker dies, tmux delivery closes the final inspection-to-submit race as far as the local tmux boundary permits, and recovery proves queued delivery plus exact-once consumption end to end.
scope: atomic or fail-closed tmux delivery commit boundary
recovery adoption, safe delivery, and exact-once event consumption tests

may: inspect and modify the uncommitted detached Runner and wakeup implementation from the rejected parent task
use tmux server-side conditional command sequencing or another narrower local mechanism to minimize the final safety-check-to-submit race
distinguish a live Runner owner from a merely live orphaned child during recovery
add deterministic dependency-injected tests for exact race and recovery paths
run focused and full deterministic verification
may_not: directly modify .opsle authority, policy, objective, historical evidence, decisions, tasks, attempts, claims, or events
modify sibling repositories or global Codex/tmux configuration
weaken generation, pane, process, composer, attached-client, delivery receipt, or claim fences
enable Claude or review, deploy, merge, push, install server-wide, or initialize another repository

relevant_context: The parent implementation and its full suite passed, but the supervisor rejected it after independent source review.

Recovery currently preserves an active claim when either attempt.pid or worker_pid is live. In detached mode only the exact live worker owns lifecycle; a live child with a dead worker is an orphan and must become UNKNOWN/intervention-required/PAUSED rather than wait indefinitely.

Current delivery performs a second inspect and then invokes literal send-keys and Enter as separate tmux processes. Replace that with the smallest server-side conditional/transactional sequence available, or fail closed and document a proven residual if tmux exposes no stronger primitive. Never clear the composer.

The final tmux decision should recheck no attached client plus stable session, pane, PID, command, and cursor immediately within the same server command sequence that submits literal input where practical. A failed predicate must report no delivery and leave the event queued without a replay hazard.
Extend tests so an alive child with a dead detached worker cannot satisfy recovery ownership, and so a client/input state change at the commit boundary produces no send.

Extend recovery coverage beyond queue adoption: a later current generation establishes safe readiness, delivers the adopted event once, consumes it once, and rejects a stale generation; duplicate recovery/drain/consume does not send again.
Keep the default detached path, explicit foreground fallback, Codex enabled, Claude disabled, review off, Gearbox required, Context Firewall required, and zero wait-induced activation semantics.
expected_deliverable: A narrow correction with deterministic evidence that dead Runner ownership fails closed, tmux delivery has a single fail-closed final commit boundary, and recovery delivers and consumes a queued event exactly once.
expected_evidence: orphaned live child plus dead worker becomes UNKNOWN/intervention-required and PAUSED
live exact worker preserves claim across recovery
final delivery predicate failure produces zero input and remains queued
safe final delivery submits literal prompt and Enter once
recovery adopts, delivers, and consumes a queued event once under the new generation
stale generation and duplicate paths do not resend or consume twice
focused tests and npm run verify pass
acceptance_criteria: only a live exact detached Runner worker constitutes lifecycle ownership during recovery
tmux final submission is guarded by an immediate server-side predicate or an equally strong fail-closed local primitive
human input is never cleared, overwritten, or submitted
unsafe final races leave durable queued/uncertain evidence and never auto-replay
recovery exact-once behavior is tested through adoption, delivery, event consumption, duplicate handling, and generation fencing
the original detached default and zero-wait properties remain intact
focused and full deterministic tests pass
prohibited_actions: accepting a child PID as a substitute for its detached Runner owner
model polling or wait-induced automatic inference
broad refactoring, history rewriting, release, deployment, merge, or global installation
operator_policy_constraints: Codex enabled with configured model and reasoning effort
